title: Turn a long parcel in place between two neighbours, then push it lengthwise into a taped bay
instruction: Get the long brown parcel into the red-taped bay, lying lengthwise with its long sides running front to back, pushed up to the stop bar, without bumping the white boxes on either side of it.
context: On induction belts and packing benches a long carton often has to be turned to fit a chute, scanner or lane while other parcels sit close beside it. Pushed at one end, a long box swings about its other end and slides into its neighbours; turning it in place takes both hands pushing its two ends in opposite directions at once, and only then does it fit through the lane's entrance.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) The long parcel: a closed brown corrugated cardboard box, 42 cm long x 14 cm deep x 10 cm tall, 800 g, lying flat with its centre 30 cm forward on the centre line and its long sides parallel to the line between the bases. Turned about its centre, its corners sweep a circle 22.1 cm in radius. (2) Two white cardboard boxes, 20 cm wide x 14 cm deep x 10 cm tall, 1.2 kg each, centred 30 cm forward and 33.3 cm left and right of the centre line: their inner faces are 2.3 cm beyond the long parcel's ends. (3) Two yellow bollards (fixed posts 3 x 3 cm, 8 cm tall) centred 48 cm forward, 20 cm left and right: 37 cm apart inside, less than the parcel's length, and 2.7 cm clear of the circle its corners sweep. (4) The bay: red tape on the table outlining a rectangle 20 cm wide (inside the tape, centred on the centre line) from 20 to 66 cm forward; it runs under the parcel's start position. (5) A dark grey stop bar (fixed, 22 cm wide x 2 cm deep x 4 cm tall) across the bay's far end, its back face 66 cm forward. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Measured from the overhead video and with a tape measure and a protractor. 1.0: the long parcel lies flat (tilted under 5 degrees) inside the bay, all four of its bottom corners within the red tape's inner edges, with its long sides within 5 degrees of front to back, everything still for 2 s; and at no time during the trial did its centre move more than 4 cm to either side of the centre line, or either white box move more than 1 cm. 0.5: those two 'at no time' conditions hold and the parcel ends flat and turned to within 10 degrees of front to back, but not inside the bay. 0.0: anything else, including any moment when the parcel slid more than 4 cm sideways or bumped a white box more than 1 cm.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed: put the three cartons back on their start positions (tape marks on the table make this quick).
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX (Isaac Sim 6.1, 20 Hz control) of a calibrated two-arm table. Simplified: the cartons are rigid, uniformly dense blocks (no flex or shifting contents), and the tape is a 0.5 mm raised strip. Loose objects get rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic); cardboard on a real table is nearer 0.4-0.5, so the pushes need less force. Dream-1 sees the 320 x 176 frames it expects; the demo video is rendered at 1280 x 720.
